question.leadin: This conflict began due to a dispute over whether Native Americans should be driven out of Virginia.
question.text: Name this 1676 rebellion against colonial governor William Berkeley. It collapsed after its namesake died of dysentery.
question.clue: This conflict began when the Occaneechees were fired upon by colonists and, in its aftermath, Charles II recalled William Berkeley to England.

swap.leadin: This woman took the name Rebecca after converting to Christianity and later married John Rolfe.
swap.text: In a heavily embellished account, John Smith credited what daughter of Chief Powhatan with saving him from an execution?
swap.clue: A governor who issued the statement "He that will not work, shall not eat" prior to the Starving Time may have been saved by this person in a ceremony.

question.leadin: This citizen of the Massachusetts Bay Colony was tried in 1637 for "traducing," or slandering, the local ministers.
question.text: Name this 17th-century woman who was sentenced in a trial overseen by John Winthrop for holding prayer sessions for women and speaking out against religious gender norms.
question.clue: This person set up a village in Portsmouth with the help of Roger Williams.

swap.leadin: Give the following about labor practices in 19th century America.
swap.text: Many Europeans migrated to the Americas by becoming this type of laborer, in which they exchanged several years of labor for their passage and were guaranteed their freedom at the end of the contract.
swap.answerHtml: indentured servants (accept word forms, like indentured servitude; prompt on servant)
swap.clue: The book's second chapter argues that the "color line" was created to pacify these people by distinguishing them from slaves. These servants worked without pay for a set amount of time.

question.leadin: With his father Increase, he actively supported smallpox inoculation.
question.text: Name this Puritan minister of the Old North Church, who claimed that "spectral evidence" was permissible during a series of 1692 events.
question.clue: A bomb was thrown through this man's window with a note attached reading "I'll inoculate you with this" after this man's slave, Onesimus, taught him about variolation and he encouraged its adoption during a smallpox epidemic.

swap.leadin: It was built by Contrecoeur in 1754 to secure the Ohio Valley during the French and Indian War.
swap.text: Name this French fort in Pennsylvania which was the target of the Braddock expedition, which turned into a fiasco. Fort Necessity was built to increase British power in the region so that an attack on this fort could occur.
swap.clue: This place was part of a series of fortifications including Fort Machault and Fort Le Boeuf.

question.leadin: Expecting to die, some defenders of this location deserted their posts and raided its rum stores to get drunk instead.
question.text: Name this military location captured during the French and Indian War by French troops who were occupying nearby Fort Duquesne. This place derived its name from the circumstances surrounding its hasty construction.
question.clue: This battle, as well as an earlier incident in a nearby Glen, would prompt the dispatch of the Braddock expedition the following year into the Ohio River Valley.

swap.leadin: An engraving of the Mystic Massacre during this conflict depicts Captain Mason making a breach in the palisade of a town, which is surrounded by archers.
swap.text: During what 1630s conflict did English settlers nearly exterminate a namesake tribe led by Sassacus?
swap.clue: The Mohawks effectively ended this war after they killed the Grand Sachem Sassacus as a sign of goodwill to the English colonists.

question.leadin: Charles Chauncy opposed this movement, led by George Whitfield among others.
question.text: Samuel Davis's Virginia preaching was the Southern impetus of what 1720s to 1740s movement?
question.clue: A speech from this movement compares its audience to "a spider, or some loathsome insect" held over a fire.

swap.leadin: Name these Spanish settlements in North America.
swap.text: This colony in Florida is the oldest surviving European establishment in mainland North America.
swap.clue: The 1763 Treaty of Paris ceded this city's colony, against which James Oglethorpe led a 1740 expedition.

question.text: The governor in Boston at the time had this last name. A woman named Anne with this surname was a religious leader who was expelled by the Puritans and settled in Portsmouth.
question.clue: A mob led by Ebenezer MacIntosh ransacked a mansion owned by a man with this surname in the aftermath of the Stamp Act.

swap.leadin: The namesakes of this land survey were hired to settle a dispute between Maryland and Pennsylvania.
swap.text: What pair of British astronomers created a namesake line that demarcates four states?
swap.clue: They fulfilled the task by laying out a series of milestones bearing coats of arms until trouble with natives forced a return to Philadelphia.

question.text: This author of New English Canaan was harassed by his Puritan neighbors after turning Merry Mount, Massachusetts into a haven of freethinking.

swap.text: During the uprising, this group of drunken rangers massacred some unarmed Conestoga Indians in Pennsylvania.
swap.clue: Their first fight was prompted by Matthew Smith's reconnaissance, and Asher Clayton and Lazarus Stewart led their two companies, which were started by Colonel Reverend John Elder.

question.text: While her husband preached about this religious group, Sarah Edwards fell into depression before her religious ecstasy. George Whitefield embraced the revivals as part of this group, unlike an "Old" predecessor.

swap.text: Previously, Malcolm had travelled to North Carolina to help the British during the Regulator War, during which citizens led by Herman Husband rebelled against this Royal Governor.
swap.clue: The Regulator movement organized in opposition to this Royal Governor of North Carolina, who built a large governmental seat in New Bern derisively known as his namesake "Palace."

question.leadin: This association created a five-member court to run its territory chaired by John Carter, and negotiated with Cherokee Indians to make the Transylvania Purchase.
question.text: Name this association which, in 1772, established an autonomous republic on the banks of the namesake river in Tennessee when they realized they were living south of the official territory of North Carolina.

swap.leadin: Though disputed by some, this man is thought to have been memorialized by a kachina called Chakwaina.
swap.text: Name this Moorish explorer, who was killed while visiting the Zuni pueblo of Hawikuh in search of Cibola ("SEE-boh-luh"). He was shipwrecked alongside Cabeza de Vaca and other members of the Narvaez ("nar-VAH-ace") Expedition.

question.text: Conflict between American settlers and Native Americans in Kentucky had earlier broken out into this 1774 war, named for a governor of Virginia.
question.clue: "Cresap's War," the Yellow Creek Massacre, and the Battle of Point Pleasant were all part of Virginia's efforts against the Shawnee and Mingo in this war, which saw the resistance led by Cornstalk and Chief Logan.

swap.leadin: Identify these figures from the age of the first Great Awakening, FTPE.
swap.text: This "grand itinerant" broke with John Wesley over Arminianism and later denied the authority of Alexander Gardiner, the rationalist Anglican commissary of South Carolina.
swap.clue: This Methodist and other itinerant preacher delivered numerous sermons during the Great Awakening. Contemporary sources note that this cross-eyed member of the "Holy Club" could make listeners weep by merely saying the word "Mesopotamia" in a booming voice.
